status: DRAFT - clinical content must be reviewed and approved by faculty before use for grading
purpose: Clinical and vital-sign criteria evaluated after each virtual patient encounter to produce an explainable score on the organizer's 7-domain Patient Encounter Performance Rubric (1-4 / N/A, max 28).
sources: evaluation rubrics/encounter_evaluation_rubric.json (7 domains, 1-4/N/A, review triggers on domains 6 and 7)
SHP_C1_Virtual_Patient_Encounter_System_Overview.pdf (feedback must cover elicited vs missed findings, sequencing, communication, explainability, faculty-defined objectives)

Reference thresholds: ACC/AHA 2017 BP categories; NCEP ATP III / 2018 ACC/AHA cholesterol guideline; NHLBI 2011 pediatric lipid cut-points (age <20); CDC/WHO BMI classes; NIAAA drinking limits; USPSTF/CDC screening recommendations

vital-signs-criteria.md and clinical-rules-sources.md (team research, 2026-10-10): V1-V4 vital rules, NEWS2 (RCP 2017), BTS 2017 O2 targets, AHA/ACC 2025 BP, ACLS 2020, SSC 2021, ADA; SEGUE (Makoul 2001) and Kalamazoo (Acad Med 2001) communication items

layers.description: Did the student ask for / obtain the clinically important findings in the approved profile?
Did the student correctly interpret vitals/labs against reference ranges and connect findings?
Did the student explain findings and next steps accurately, in plain language, and check understanding?
Did the student screen red flags, safety-net, avoid unsafe advice and avoid inventing facts?
Universal interview behaviours (opening, empathy, cues, closure).

critical.note: Missing any critical item caps the mapped domain at 2.

scoring_model.domain_mapping_rule: Each criterion carries a rubric domain id (1-7). Domain coverage = sum(weights met) / sum(weights applicable) for that domain.

caps_and_gates.rule: If any 'critical' criterion mapped to a domain is not met, that domain score is capped at 2.
If any unsafe_action is detected, domain 7 = 1 (and domain 6 = 1 if the unsafe action is a clinical-reasoning error). This triggers faculty review.
A domain with no applicable criteria in this case is scored N/A and excluded from available points.

output.review_required: true if domain 6 or 7 scores 1, or any unsafe_action detected
output.status: auto_scored_pending_faculty_review - the automated score is a draft; faculty confirm via the existing review screen

scoring_model.explainability_contract: Every criterion result must include: met (true/false), evidence turn ids + quote (or 'no evidence'), and the criterion's feedback_if_missed. No score without evidence.

reference_ranges._note: Adult resting values unless stated. Units must be confirmed per case - the source CSV omits lipid units; mg/dL is assumed and must be faculty-confirmed.

blood_pressure_mmHg.source: AHA/ACC 2025 (categories unchanged from 2017); target <130/80 for most adults
blood_pressure_mmHg.severe_hypertension_or_crisis: SBP >180 and/or DBP >120 -> urgent assessment; emergency if new chest pain, dyspnoea, neuro deficit, vision change, confusion

temperature.older_adult_ltc_fever: single oral >37.8 C, repeated >37.2 C, or >1.1 C above baseline (IDSA)

reference_ranges.bmi_under_20: Use CDC BMI-for-age percentiles: >=85th overweight, >=95th obesity. A BMI of 32 at age 18 is >=95th percentile (obesity).

ldl.very_high: >=190 (severe hypercholesterolaemia: high-intensity statin indicated without risk calculation; consider familial hypercholesterolaemia)

reference_ranges.metabolic_syndrome_atp3: Any 3 of: waist >40 in (men)/>35 in (women); TG >=150; HDL <40 (men)/<50 (women); BP >=130/85 or treated; fasting glucose >=100
reference_ranges.alcohol_niaaa: Heavy drinking - men: >4 drinks/day or >14/week; women: >3/day or >7/week
reference_ranges.sodium: General limit <2,300 mg/day; AHA ideal <1,500 mg/day for most adults with hypertension. 1 tsp table salt ~= 2,300 mg sodium; salt is ~40% sodium.
reference_ranges.fibre_dga: ~14 g per 1,000 kcal; males 14-18 ~31 g/day, males 19-30 ~34 g/day
reference_ranges.heart_failure_terms: NYHA = functional CLASS I-IV; ACC/AHA = STAGE A-D. 'NYHA Stage C' mixes the two systems and should be flagged.
reference_ranges.orthostatic_hypotension: SBP drop >=20 or DBP drop >=10 within 3 min of standing
reference_ranges.pediatric_note: For age <18 use PALS age bands and AAP 2017 BP percentiles (see vital-signs-criteria.md section 3); pregnancy uses obstetric thresholds (severe >=160/110) and MEOWS, not NEWS2.

universal_criteria.criterion: Introduces self by name and role
universal_criteria.feedback_if_missed: Start by giving your name and role so the patient knows who they are talking to.
universal_criteria.framework: SEGUE Set the stage; Kalamazoo Opens

universal_criteria.criterion: Confirms patient identity (name) respectfully
cues: what would you like me to call
can you tell me your name
universal_criteria.feedback_if_missed: Confirm the patient's name and how they'd like to be addressed.

universal_criteria.criterion: States purpose/agenda and elicits the patient's main concern with an open question
cues: what would you like to focus
universal_criteria.feedback_if_missed: Set the agenda early: explain why you're there and ask an open question about their main concern.
universal_criteria.framework: SEGUE Set the stage; Kalamazoo Opens

universal_criteria.criterion: Acknowledges emotion or difficulty with an empathic statement
universal_criteria.feedback_if_missed: When the patient shares a concern or feeling, name it and acknowledge it before moving on.

universal_criteria.criterion: Uses non-judgemental language about lifestyle, weight, adherence or substance use (absence of blaming language)
universal_criteria.feedback_if_missed: Avoid blaming language; ask about barriers instead of labelling the patient.

universal_criteria.criterion: Uses open-ended questions before closed questions
universal_criteria.feedback_if_missed: Begin topics with open questions ('Tell me about...') and narrow down afterwards.

universal_criteria.criterion: Asks about current medications and adherence
universal_criteria.feedback_if_missed: Always review current medications and how they are actually being taken.

universal_criteria.criterion: Asks about allergies
universal_criteria.feedback_if_missed: Ask about medication and other allergies.

universal_criteria.criterion: Asks about relevant past medical and family history
universal_criteria.feedback_if_missed: Explore past medical and family history relevant to the presenting problem.

universal_criteria.criterion: Asks about social context (living situation, work, support, substances)
universal_criteria.feedback_if_missed: Ask about home, work and support - it shapes what plan is realistic.

universal_criteria.criterion: Requests or reviews vital signs / available measurements (BP, HR, RR, temp, SpO2, weight/BMI)
universal_criteria.feedback_if_missed: Review the available vital signs and measurements in the chart before forming a plan.

universal_criteria.criterion: Follows up on something the patient said (reflects/clarifies)
universal_criteria.feedback_if_missed: Pick up on the patient's own words and follow up ('You mentioned...').

universal_criteria.criterion: Asks for the patient's ideas, concerns or expectations
universal_criteria.feedback_if_missed: Ask what the patient thinks is going on, what worries them and what they hope for.

universal_criteria.criterion: Checks understanding (teach-back or explicit check)
universal_criteria.feedback_if_missed: Use teach-back: 'To make sure I explained it well, can you tell me in your own words...'
universal_criteria.framework: SEGUE Give information; Kalamazoo Shares information

universal_criteria.criterion: Involves the patient in decisions / explores readiness and preferences
universal_criteria.feedback_if_missed: Offer options and ask what feels realistic, rather than prescribing a single plan.

universal_criteria.criterion: Summarises key findings back to the patient
cues: let me make sure i have
universal_criteria.feedback_if_missed: Summarise the key findings before moving to explanation or plan.

universal_criteria.criterion: Acknowledges uncertainty or missing data rather than guessing
universal_criteria.feedback_if_missed: Name what is still unknown and what would be needed to find out.

universal_criteria.criterion: Closes with a clear next step / follow-up plan
universal_criteria.feedback_if_missed: End with a clear, shared next step and follow-up.
universal_criteria.framework: SEGUE End the encounter; Kalamazoo Closes

universal_criteria.criterion: Safety-nets: tells patient which symptoms need urgent care
universal_criteria.feedback_if_missed: Safety-net: tell the patient which warning signs should prompt urgent care.

universal_criteria.criterion: States limits of own role / defers to supervising clinician where appropriate
universal_criteria.feedback_if_missed: Be clear about your role's limits and who will make final decisions.

universal_criteria.criterion: Asks 'anything else?' before closing
universal_criteria.feedback_if_missed: Before closing, ask 'Is there anything else you wanted to discuss?'

universal_criteria.criterion: Logical sequence: opening -> concern/HPI -> history (meds/allergies/social) -> summary/explanation -> closure
universal_criteria.feedback_if_missed: Follow a clear structure: open, explore, gather history, summarise/explain, then close.

universal_criteria.criterion: Asks about medications and allergies before suggesting any treatment
universal_criteria.feedback_if_missed: Check medications and allergies before suggesting any treatment.

unsafe_actions.description: Advises stopping or changing a prescribed medication or dose without the prescriber
Misinterprets a clearly abnormal value as normal (e.g. calls BP 155/110 or LDL 195 'normal' / 'nothing to worry about')
Gives false reassurance or overstates certainty about diagnosis/prognosis
States clinical facts not in the approved profile as if they were the patient's results
Stigmatising or discriminatory remarks (sexuality, ethnicity, weight, substance use, immigration status)
Misses an explicit red-flag statement from the patient without acting/escalating

6ca4cbf9-14ef-427c-b87c-bc9d34ce02b8.name: Yvette Armstrong
6ca4cbf9-14ef-427c-b87c-bc9d34ce02b8.summary: Newly diagnosed Stage 2 hypertension; BMI 34; confused about sodium vs salt; low understanding of prior explanation.

expected_interpretation.bp: 155/110 = Stage 2 hypertension (SBP >=140 and DBP >=90); not in crisis range (>180/>120).

criteria.criterion: Obtains/reviews BP reading and BMI
criteria.feedback_if_missed: Review her BP (155/110) and BMI (34) - they drive the whole teaching plan.

criteria.criterion: Asks what she already understands about her diagnosis
criteria.feedback_if_missed: Ask what she was told and understood before explaining - she said she didn't understand her doctor.

criteria.criterion: Explores current diet / salt use / food sources (processed food, eating out)
criteria.feedback_if_missed: Ask about her typical meals and where her sodium comes from.

criteria.criterion: Asks about BP-related symptoms (headache, vision change, chest pain, shortness of breath)
criteria.feedback_if_missed: Screen for symptoms that would make this urgent.

criteria.criterion: Asks about other CV risk factors (diabetes, kidney disease, smoking, family history) and medications
criteria.feedback_if_missed: Ask about other cardiovascular risk factors and current medications.

criteria.criterion: Correctly identifies 155/110 as Stage 2 (high) hypertension
criteria.feedback_if_missed: Explicitly interpret the reading: 155/110 is Stage 2 hypertension (>=140/90).

criteria.criterion: Links excess weight and sodium to blood pressure
criteria.feedback_if_missed: Connect the dots: sodium and extra weight both raise BP.

criteria.criterion: Explains hypertension in plain language (no jargon)
criteria.feedback_if_missed: Explain hypertension in everyday words (e.g. 'blood pushing too hard against the vessel walls').

criteria.criterion: Clarifies sodium vs salt and gives a numeric limit (<2,300 mg/day; ideally ~1,500 mg)
criteria.feedback_if_missed: Clarify that salt contains sodium and give a concrete daily limit (about 1 teaspoon of salt = 2,300 mg).

criteria.criterion: Teaches food-label reading or practical swaps (DASH-style)
criteria.feedback_if_missed: Give practical tools: reading the sodium line on labels, DASH-style swaps.

criteria.criterion: Explains benefit of modest weight loss (5-10%)
criteria.feedback_if_missed: Explain that even modest (5-10%) weight loss lowers blood pressure.

criteria.criterion: Safety-nets for severe BP / symptoms (>=180/120, chest pain, neuro or vision change) and suggests home BP monitoring
criteria.feedback_if_missed: Advise home BP monitoring and when to seek emergency care.

profile_gaps_to_acknowledge: No HR, other vitals, labs (kidney function, glucose, lipids) or medication list in profile

b5814549-fd2b-42a2-af78-9b681ad6f268.name: Omar Sinclair
b5814549-fd2b-42a2-af78-9b681ad6f268.summary: Dyslipidaemia (TC 260, LDL 195, HDL 30), BMI 29, waist 43 in, uncomfortable with medications.

profile_values.units: not supplied - assume mg/dL, faculty to confirm

expected_interpretation.ldl: 195 = very high (>=190): statin indicated per 2018 ACC/AHA without risk calculation; evaluate for familial hypercholesterolaemia
expected_interpretation.metsyn: 2 of 5 ATP III criteria known (waist, HDL); TG, BP and fasting glucose missing to decide

criteria.criterion: Reviews lipid panel (TC, LDL, HDL)
criteria.feedback_if_missed: Review his lipid panel - LDL 195 is the central finding.

criteria.criterion: Reviews BMI and waist circumference
criteria.feedback_if_missed: Review BMI (29) and waist (43 in) - both add cardiometabolic risk.

criteria.criterion: Explores his concerns about taking medication
criteria.feedback_if_missed: Explore why he is uncomfortable with medication before recommending one.

criteria.criterion: Asks about family history of early heart disease / high cholesterol
criteria.feedback_if_missed: LDL >=190 raises suspicion of familial hypercholesterolaemia - ask about family history.

criteria.criterion: Asks about other ASCVD risk factors: smoking, BP, diabetes, activity, diet
criteria.feedback_if_missed: Ask about smoking, BP, diabetes, diet and activity to estimate overall risk.

criteria.criterion: Identifies LDL 195 as very high and HDL 30 as low
criteria.feedback_if_missed: Interpret explicitly: LDL 195 is very high (>=190) and HDL 30 is low (<40).

criteria.criterion: Notes missing data needed (triglycerides, glucose/A1c, BP) for full risk / metabolic-syndrome assessment
criteria.feedback_if_missed: Point out what's missing: TG, glucose and BP are needed to complete his risk picture.

criteria.criterion: Explains LDL ('bad') vs HDL ('good') in plain language
criteria.feedback_if_missed: Explain LDL vs HDL simply - he specifically needs this.

criteria.criterion: Explains the purpose of statins and benefits/side-effects honestly, respecting his choice

criteria.criterion: Gives realistic diet steps (less saturated/trans fat, more soluble fibre, weight/waist reduction, activity)

criteria.criterion: Does not tell him diet alone is sufficient at LDL >=190; defers prescribing decision to prescriber
criteria.feedback_if_missed: At LDL >=190 guidelines recommend a statin - don't imply diet alone is enough; refer the decision to the prescriber.

vital_sign_rules._note: Generic templates - generated automatically from whatever vitals a case contains, so they work for any patient faculty create. Faculty may override thresholds per case (e.g. COPD SpO2 baseline).

per_abnormal_vital.name: Recognized
per_abnormal_vital.met_when: Student names/acknowledges the abnormal value or rechecks it
per_abnormal_vital.feedback_if_missed: You did not comment on the abnormal {vital} ({value}). Name it and say why it matters.

per_abnormal_vital.name: Assessed
per_abnormal_vital.met_when: >=2 items from the abnormality's assess list asked/ordered
per_abnormal_vital.feedback_if_missed: Follow up the abnormal {vital} with targeted questions: {assess}.

per_abnormal_vital.name: Treated / escalated
per_abnormal_vital.met_when: States an expected first action from the abnormality's treat list

per_abnormal_vital.name: Reassessed
per_abnormal_vital.met_when: Requests repeat vitals after a V3 action
per_abnormal_vital.feedback_if_missed: Recheck the vitals after your intervention.

encounter_wide.name: Full set obtained
encounter_wide.met_when: HR, BP, RR, SpO2, temperature all reviewed (+ pain/glucose when relevant)

encounter_wide.name: Early-warning escalation
encounter_wide.applies_when: adult, non-pregnant, NEWS2 >=5 or any single parameter = 3
encounter_wide.met_when: Student escalates (senior / rapid response / higher acuity)

treat: ECG + escalate if HR >=150 or unstable
no organ damage: resume/adjust oral meds, recheck, follow-up (rapid IV lowering = not met)
organ damage: emergency, monitored IV therapy
prescriber to start/adjust therapy (often two drugs for stage 2)
15-20 g fast glucose (IV dextrose/glucagon if cannot swallow)
